key_insight: Generating plausible protein–ligand binding poses is not enough—choosing the right one remains difficult. Pyrite introduces 1,500 pose-pair comparisons, and expert chemists using 3D visualization and physics-based scores perform near chance.
problem_solved: The paper addresses how to evaluate systems that rank candidate protein–ligand binding poses generated by modern cofolding models.
method: Introduce a pairwise pose-ranking benchmark with 1,500 pose pairs spanning diverse protein–ligand complexes.
Frame ranking as a choice between two candidate binding poses.
Evaluate expert chemists equipped with 3D visualization tools and physics-based scores to assess the task’s difficulty.
impact: Pyrite provides a benchmark for testing AI pose-ranking systems in a drug-discovery setting. Near-chance expert performance highlights the need for stronger methods to interpret structural and chemical evidence.
visual_elements: Side-by-side 3D views of two ligand poses inside the same protein binding pocket.
Workflow diagram: candidate poses → pairwise comparison → pose selection.
Benchmark overview highlighting 1,500 pose pairs across diverse complexes.
Qualitative comparison showing expert performance near a chance baseline, without inventing exact scores.
paper_title: Pyrite: Building and Benchmarking Protein-Ligand Pose Ranking Agents
paper_authors: Megha Srivastava, Michael H. Lim, Allison M. Keys, Pranav Murugan, Nate Gruver
